summary: Iter 28 backend testing — recurring events, /api/health, scale-readiness rate limits. Wrote /app/backend/tests/test_iter28_recurring_events_health_ratelimits.py covering all 14 requested cases. ALL 14 PASS (14/14 = 100%). Key verifications: (1) Weekly recurrence_count=3 creates master + 3 children on 7-day cadence, all share series_id, master.series_master=True, children False, series_event_ids length=4. (2) Monthly 2026-01-31 + recurrence_count=2 clamps correctly to 2026-02-28 and 2026-03-31 (Feb-end clamp confirmed). (3) Fortnightly recurrence_count=2 → 3 events 14d apart. (4) One-off (no recurrence) flow regression: exactly 1 event stored, recurrence/series_id null, series_master False, series_event_ids=[id]. (5) recurrence_count=99 caps at 25 additional → 26 total. (6) GET /api/events surfaces recurrence field on children. (7) /api/health returns 200 {status:'ok', db:'up'} and 'Indexes verified: 14 / 14 targets' log line confirmed in /var/log/supervisor/backend.err.log. (8) Rate limits all fire exactly at boundary with 429 + Retry-After header: notices 6→7, flutters 20→21, reports 10→11, events 8→9 per host. (9) Existing RSVP works on one-off and recurring child events; PATCH host-edit on a recurring child persists (time change verified via GET).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 6075 lines — well over the 700-line guideline. Recurrence helpers (_add_days, _add_months, _next_occurrence) plus rate_limit could comfortably move into modules (events/recurrence.py, common/rate_limit.py). Not a regression; flagged for future cleanup.

rate_limit is in-process only — multiple backend pods would each have their own bucket. The code comment already calls this out (Tier-1 by design, swap to Redis at Tier-2). Just noting it explicitly so it isn't forgotten when scaling out.
Rate-limit retry hint uses time.monotonic-based math, so Retry-After is accurate even across NTP clock skews — nice. No issue.

No upper validation on recurrence_count input type — if a host posts a string like '5x' it silently falls back to 3. Behaviour is safe (caught by int() in try/except), but a 400 would be a more honest API contract.

Master event sets recurrence_count in its stored doc (Event model inherits the field from EventCreateBody via body.dict). The exclude={'recurrence_count'} on master_dict prevents that — verified by reading the code path. Good.
seed_data_creation: Test created 49 TEST_iter28_ events, 6 notices, 10 reports, 20 flutters during the run. All cleaned up post-run via direct Mongo delete (titles/notes/messages prefixed TEST_iter28_).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Rate-limit tests restart the backend (sudo supervisorctl restart backend) immediately before each rate-limit boundary check to start with empty in-process buckets. Keep this pattern if extending — recurring or notices/reports tests that share the same identifier as a prior rate-limit test will trip the 429 cap unless the bucket is reset. /api/health is the right readiness probe to wait on after a restart (already used by the test helper).
